plan_review.notes: Alt A: runtime-only bespoke moving saw state — rejected because it would duplicate projectile/return cleanup instead of reusing existing returning-projectile lifecycle. Alt B: fully generic path-phase runtime overhaul before landing Fizzwick — rejected because it expands scope beyond the bounded issue. Chosen: keep typed mob-ability runtime as authoritative committed-path state, extend public cue/geometry phases beyond telegraph, and reuse/extend returning projectile lifecycle for outbound/hold/return/re-catch. Added clipped endpoint semantics, pass-aware hit latching, Queen/Panda regression coverage, explicit default-off zero-casts proof, and process notes for issue-comment 403 + registry override.

rounds.notes: Finding 1: lane damage can bleed through walls near edges — accepted with ADR-0076 DEC-004 documentation as an arena-only ability where open-arena use is the intended deployment. Finding 2: clearMobAbility during active phase permanently disables boss ability for the encounter — fixed by replacing clearMobAbility call in updateActiveState with beginCooldownAfterActive to preserve ability registration.

Finding 1: Conflict markers in HEAD (critical) — already resolved in working tree by conflict-resolution agent; committed in this push. Finding 2: Test for target-despawn during active cast asserted old clearMobAbility behavior (byEntity.has=false) instead of new beginCooldownAfterActive behavior (phase=cooldown, registration preserved) — test updated to assert inst.phase==='cooldown' and byEntity.has===true. Finding 3: beginCooldownAfterActive fired recatch VFX at lane origin even during early abort when saw is mid-lane — fixed to use inst.activeState.projectileX/Y when available, falling back to geometry.originX/Y for normal completion.
